Container.Name: messages-server
Container.Overview: Message Link Server. Keeps your messaging accounts connected on this server so Message Link on your PCs can use them over your home network. A PC asks to join and you approve it on the server's page, or it pairs once with the code in this container's log and checks the fingerprint beside it. Nothing is served without pairing. The keys and this server's Messenger history live in the Docker volume messages-server-keys, off every share; the data folder holds only sealed data that is useless without them. Losing the keys volume loses that history and means signing in and pairing again, so back it up (README, Backups).
Container.Requires: Build the image on this server first: docker build -f docker/messages-server/Dockerfile -t messages-server:local . (from a copy of the Message Link source). Create the data and backups folders owned by 2787:2787 with mode 700 before the first start.

Config.Name: Port
Config.Description: The one port the Message Link app connects to (TLS). Nothing else is published. As a bare port it is published on every interface, a VPN's included; prefer the install script, which publishes on the LAN address you give it.

Config.Name: Data
Config.Description: Saved sign-ins, history and paired devices, encrypted and useless without the keys volume. Must be owned by 2787:2787 (the user in Extra Parameters), mode 700.

Config.Name: Backups
Config.Description: Where the server writes its own backups (README, Backups): a folder on the backups share by default. Must be owned by 2787:2787, mode 700. A backup holds the history and the server's identity but no service sign-in.

Config.Name: Resume sign-ins at start
Config.Description: 1 resumes the accounts signed in on this server when the container starts. 0 starts with none connected.

Config.Name: Server page password
Config.Description: The password of the server's own page: open https://(this server):8787/ in a browser to approve devices that ask to join, see its status and devices, and make a pairing code. 12 to 128 characters, with no double spaces, no spaces at either end and no &-codes (Unraid would change those). Unraid shows it in the docker command it prints when you apply or update the container, so use a password you use nowhere else. Empty: the page's first visit asks for the setup code from this container's log and sets its password there. Set here, it wins over that one. Changing it signs every browser out.

Config.Name: Google Messages and Voice
Config.Description: 1 runs Google Messages and Google Voice beside the server's own Google Chrome.

Config.Name: Google through Chrome
Config.Description: Leave at 1: Google is signed in by hand in the server's own Chrome, which keeps the sign-in fresh.

Config.Name: Chrome on its own display
Config.Description: Leave at 1: Chrome draws on a virtual display inside the container.

Config.Name: Network of its own
Config.Description: 1 on the bridge network: the container has a network of its own, so the page may show Google's sign-in from the server's Chrome. Set 0 with host networking.

Config.Name: Chrome without its sandbox
Config.Description: 1 runs Chrome without its own sandbox, which a container with every capability dropped cannot give it. Chrome loads only Google's sign-in pages. The project's README explains how to run with the sandbox instead.

Config.Name: Reach from your tailnet
Config.Description: 1 puts the server on your Tailscale network as a machine of its own, so your phone reaches it through Tailscale built into Message Link while the port above stays on your home network. The first start prints a Tailscale sign-in link in this container's log: open it and sign in. In Tailscale's admin page, turn off key expiry for the server. Its identity is kept in the keys volume (README, Your tailnet).

Config.Name: Tailscale auth key
Config.Description: Optional, with Reach from your tailnet at 1: a Tailscale auth key (tskey-auth-..., from Tailscale's admin console, Settings, Keys) that signs the server in by itself the first time, instead of the sign-in link. Only the server's tailnet door is given it. A tagged key makes a tagged machine, and the server then lets in every device your access rules let through, not only your own (README, Your tailnet). Clear it once the server is signed in.

Config.Name: Tailnet name
Config.Description: The server's name on your tailnet: lowercase letters, digits and dashes.

Config.Name: Data folder in the container
Config.Description: Leave as /data, the folder mapped above.

Config.Name: Keys folder in the container
Config.Description: Leave as /keys, the volume in Extra Parameters.
